title: Munster, Indiana: the Brass Tavern and the House Behind It

sources.what: the tavern was 'a large, two-story, flat-roofed frame building'; 'The only telegraph office in the region was housed there'; 'it was to the tavern that news of the assassination of Lincoln first came'; it 'burned, in November, 1909'; 'the beams smouldered for days after the rest of the house was burned'; 'we built our present home several hundred feet to the rear'; 'a small, open front porch the width of the house'
sources.who: Wilhelmine Stallbohm Kaske, 'Early Days in Munster', History of Lake County vol. XI (Lake County Historical Association, 1934)

sources.what: Gibson 'built a log stagecoach inn' in 1837; the Brasses 'took over the property in 1845'; telegraph 'Set up in 1859', 'first news of Abraham Lincoln's assassination'; 'in 1909, the inn was lost to a fire'; the Kaske House 'built behind the old Brass Tavern/Stallbohm Inn'; 'now the Munster History Museum'; Heritage Park
sources.who: Brass Tavern / Kaske House historical marker, Munster (2023), on HMdb.org

sources.what: Lincoln news 'first reached the Calumet region on the inn's telegraph line'; inn stood 'just north of the present house, close to Ridge Road'; house 'built for the Kaskes by the Kooy brothers'; 'An open porch extended the width of the main facade'; limestone foundation; Jerkin-head roof
sources.who: National Register of Historic Places nomination, Stallbohm Barn-Kaske House (1996)

sources.what: 'Built in 1845 and originally named the Brass Tavern'; 'In 1909, much of the original structure was destroyed by fire'; Kaske House in Munster, 'originally an inn and now a museum'
sources.who: James B. Lane, Northwest Indiana historian (2016)

sources.what: Mike McDowell of Indiana Ghost Trackers described a spirit whispering 'this is my bedroom – get out' at the Kaske home in Munster
sources.who: GreatNews.Life, 'Northwest Indiana A Hotbed for Haunted Folklore' (2014)

sources.what: 'Witnesses have reported ... a presence in the bedroom, cold spots, footsteps, and crashing sounds'

beats.text: This is my bedroom. Get out. A ghost tour operator says a voice once whispered that inside a house in Munster, Indiana.
beats.label: MUNSTER, INDIANA
beats.credit: Legend: Mike McDowell, Indiana Ghost Trackers (GreatNews.Life)

beats.text: The house stands behind the spot where the Brass Tavern stood, an old inn on Ridge Road.
beats.label: THE BRASS TAVERN
beats.credit: History: Wilhelmine Stallbohm Kaske (1934); National Register

beats.text: A new family bought it in 1864. Their daughter later wrote that it housed the region's only telegraph office, and that news of Lincoln's assassination first reached the area there.
In the fall of 1909, the old tavern burned. She wrote that the beams smoldered for days.
beats.credit: Wilhelmine Stallbohm Kaske, 'Early Days in Munster' (1934)

beats.text: Her family built a new house behind the ruins. Today it's a museum in Heritage Park.
beats.label: THE KASKE HOUSE

beats.text: One haunted-places listing reports footsteps, cold spots, and a presence in the bedroom. That part is legend. The fire was real.
beats.label: WHAT ONE LISTING REPORTS

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

notes: Fact-check 1 (Nov. 17, 2026): no source says the tavern was built in 1845 (Gibson's log inn 1837; the Brasses took over in 1845; Kaske and the National Register put Brass's new inn about 1855), so the line says 'took it over in 1845'. The house's year is 1909 or 1910 by source, so no year. The 'get out' quote is Mike McDowell's account of his tours, in one article; the footsteps/cold spots/presence are one reader-submitted listing. The tavern had a full-width open porch. munsterhistory.org loops between https and http and can't be fetched. Fact-check 2: 'took it over in 1845' rests on the marker alone and the frame inn dates to about 1855, so the date and the stagecoach came out; 'the owners' daughter' right after the Brass name sounded like the Brasses' daughter (she was the Stallbohms', who bought it in 1864), so the line now says 'A new family bought it in 1864. Their daughter later wrote'. The names Stallbohm and Kaske are on screen and in credits but not spoken (local pronunciation not confirmed).
